calculation.activity: LIQUID-only equilibria; reference pure liquid at T
calculation.field_map: own pycalphad equilibrium grid, dx 0.01 (ends 1e-5), dT 10 K; fields = connected cells with equal labelled assemblage
calculation.formation: single-phase equilibrium at 298.15 K; HM relative to SER
calculation.formation_v2: single-phase equilibrium at the phase's low-T composition, 298.15 K; dfS = S - sum x_i S_i(SER); SER entropies from unary equilibria at 298.15 K
calculation.liquid_mixing: calculate HM/GM of LIQUID minus linear pure-liquid reference

mixing_table.partials: H_i - H_i(pure liquid) from central differences of the integral HM_MIX (h = 1e-4)
mixing_table.reference: pure liquid A and B at T

calculation.order_disorder: composition sets of phases with equivalent sublattices reported in the disordered state are renamed to the disordered lattice phase (e.g. L12_FCC -> FCC_A1)

unit_conversions.formula_unit: value per formula unit = value per mole of atoms x atoms per formula unit

v2.grid: same composition-set-aware grid as the field map
v2.stability_limits: grid limit snapped to an invariant/congruent/melting T within one grid step, otherwise bisection to 0.01 K at a fixed composition

sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Al–Si binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset AlSi-12Tan.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L → (Al) + (Si), lies at 850 K.
The Al–Si system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as simple eutectic.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of Y. Tang, Y. Du, L. Zhang, X. Yuan, G. Kaptay, Thermochim. Acta, 527, 131-42(2012). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
The melting point of Al reproduced by the dataset is 935 K.
The eutectic reaction L → (Al) + (Si) is calculated at 850 K, with L at x(Si) = 0.121.
Table 1 compares the calculated temperatures with experimental values from the literature [3–5]; in this synthetic document those values and references are fictitious.
The solubility of Si in (Al) reaches a mole fraction of 0.017 at 850 K.
At 1750 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its minimum, −3.46 kJ/mol, at x(Si) = 0.520.
For the equiatomic liquid at 1750 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −13346 J/mol.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
